text: What is the status of optical random-access memory (RAM) in photonic computing?
choices: Optical RAM already matches DRAM in both density and rewrite endurance
Quantum optical memories serve directly as a photonic computer's working memory
Phase-change optical memory offers effectively unlimited rewrite endurance
There is no true photonic RAM; storage means volatile delay lines, short-lived cavities, or slow phase-change materials, so memory stays electronic
explanation: There is no photonic equivalent of RAM: the options are volatile delay lines, short-lived resonant cavities, or non-volatile but slow phase-change materials (endurance only about 10^6 to 10^9 writes), so every practical photonic computer keeps its memory in electronics. PCM endurance is far from unlimited, and quantum optical memories buffer single photons, a different job, not a classical working set.
